q: How was the holdout-2025q4 evaluation set built, and when was it frozen?
a: A random 30% of accounts, stratified by tenure band, with Oct-Dec 2025 observation dates (1.2M accounts) and never used for training; frozen 2026-09-04, split by nb/make_holdout.ipynb.

q: How is the 90-day churn label in cards.churn_labels defined, and who maintains it?
a: It is a 90-day churn flag per account and month-end observation date: the account has no card spend for the 90 days after the observation date. The retention-labels job builds it from cards.txn_daily, and data-eng-cards maintains it.

q: Which function computes the churn-2026 decision metric, and with what k?
a: recall@10 is computed by nb/metrics.py::recall_at_k with k=0.10, giving the share of 90-day churners caught in the top 10% of scores.

q: What are the inputs, windows and code location of feat-utilization-v1?
a: Three util_ columns of balance divided by credit_limit over 1, 3 and 6 months, using balance and credit_limit from cards.txn_daily with all windows ending on the observation date; code is features/utilization_v1.py.

q: How was the exp-015 tenure split defined, and which notebook holds it?
a: holdout-2025q4 was split at 6 months of tenure into new accounts (n=168k, 14%) and accounts with tenure of 6 months or more (n=1.03M); the notebook is nb/exp015_tenure.ipynb.

q: What came of the exp-017 leak check run on 2026-10-28?
a: Removing post-period days took AUC from 0.81 to 0.74; the finding was followed on 2026-10-29 by the post-period-leak conclusion that the velocity aggregation leaks the target, and on 2026-10-30 Sam Lee decided to rebuild velocity as feat-velocity-v3 and retire v2.

q: What did the 2026-10-26 leak review start from, and where did its September data question end up?
a: It began a review of the exp-014 velocity columns and the team asked data-eng-cards about the short September partitions; the September backfill of cards.txn_daily (ticket DE-4411) finished on 2026-10-27.

q: What led to the 0.20 and 0.50 risk-tier cuts, and what budget were they fitted to?
a: Maya Ortiz asked on 2026-10-05 for three tiers from churn-xgb-v2 scores (call, email, nothing); the budget allowed calls for 4% of the book and emails for 12%, and the 2026-10-08 decision with retention set the cuts at 0.50 and 0.20.

q: What did the exp-011 logistic baseline establish for the later experiments?
a: It set the reference model: logistic regression on 14 account-level features with no velocity or utilization; exp-014 added 30-day velocity to that set, and the lift came mostly from vel_ratio_30_90.

q: What led to the new-accounts finding, and which options were put forward?
a: exp-015 (2026-10-10) split churn-xgb-v2 at 6 months of tenure, and finding-new-accounts (2026-10-12) then noted that new accounts are 14% of the book and 21% of churners with too little history for velocity or utilization; options were a tenure-specific model or routing them to onboarding, owned by Priya Nair.

q: Which churn models depend on feat-utilization-v1, and what did the 2026-10-29 check mean for them?
a: churn-xgb-v2 and churn-xgb-v3 both use feat-utilization-v1; the 2026-10-29 check found no post-period days in its three util_ columns, so it stays unchanged in v3.

q: What does feat-velocity-v3 read from, and which model uses it?
a: It reads cards.txn_daily (code features/velocity_v3.py) and builds 6 vel_ columns from the 30 days before the observation date plus their ratio to the prior 90-day average; churn-xgb-v3 uses it.

q: What does the nightly offers.tier_matrix assignment depend on?
a: It applies the risk-tier cuts (0.50 for call, 0.20 for email) to churn-xgb-v2 scores, and those cuts stay fixed until the open q-recalibrate-tiers question is answered.

q: What evidence does the post-period leak conclusion rest on?
a: On exp-014 and exp-017, where removing post-period days took holdout-2025q4 AUC from 0.81 to 0.74, and on the eda_velocity notebook cells 12-18, which were kept as evidence on 2026-10-29.

q: What does the monthly retrain decision depend on, and what does it leave unchanged?
a: It is built from churn-xgb-v3 and dec-risk-tiers, retraining monthly on the latest 9 observation months of cards.churn_labels, while the 0.20 and 0.50 risk-tier cuts stay until q-recalibrate-tiers is answered.

q: What training window does the current monthly churn-xgb retrain use?
a: The latest 9 observation months of cards.churn_labels, per the 2026-10-30 decision; churn-xgb-v3 itself was fit on 2025-01 to 2025-09.

q: Which velocity feature version is current, and how does its window differ from v2?
a: feat-velocity-v3, decided 2026-10-30, supersedes v2 and keeps the same 6 vel_ columns, but its window is the 30 days before the observation date, where v2 used the 30 days around it.

q: Is the 0.52 recall@10 reported for churn-xgb-v2 still a valid figure to quote?
a: No: the 0.52 came from the post-period leak. The honest figure is churn-xgb-v3's recall@10 of 0.43 on holdout-2025q4 (n=1.2M, 2026-10-30), with monthly cohorts at 0.40 to 0.45.

q: Which txn partitions were still being backfilled as of 2026-10-30?
a: The log only says October partitions (year not stated) of cards.txn_daily were being backfilled on 2026-10-30; the September 2025 gap had already been fixed on 2026-10-27.

q: What is the current status of the September 2025 cards.txn_daily gap, and which v2 numbers does it affect?
a: It is fixed: the backfill finished 2026-10-27 and row counts match the ledger within 0.1%. Any v2 numbers computed before 2026-10-27 used about 6% fewer September transactions.

q: What AUC and recall@10 did the logistic baseline reach on holdout-2025q4, and what was n and the feature count?
a: AUC 0.71 and recall@10 0.29 on holdout-2025q4, n=1.2M, with 14 account-level features (no velocity or utilization), reported 2026-09-15.

q: How many trees and what depth did the exp-014 XGBoost use, and what AUC and recall@10 did it reach on holdout-2025q4 (n)?
a: 400 trees at depth 6; AUC 0.81 and recall@10 0.52 on holdout-2025q4, n=1.2M, reported 2026-09-25.

q: What AUC and recall@10 did exp-017 report on holdout-2025q4 with post-period days removed, and at what n?
a: AUC 0.74 and recall@10 0.41 on holdout-2025q4, n=1.2M, reported 2026-10-28.

q: What recall@10 did churn-xgb-v3 get on the December 2025 observation cohort of holdout-2025q4?
a: 0.40 for December (October 0.45, November 0.43), from re-scoring holdout-2025q4 with n=1.2M overall, recorded 2026-10-30.

q: What share of the book sits in the call and email tiers at the 0.20 and 0.50 cuts?
a: The call tier (score at or above 0.50) is 3.8% of the book and the email tier (0.20 to 0.50) is 11.6%, both on churn-xgb-v2 scores; the notes give no n for the book count.

q: Why is recall@10 used to judge decisions rather than AUC?
a: Retention can call only 10% of the book each month, so the question is how many 90-day churners land in the top 10% of scores; AUC is reported alongside but decisions use recall@10.

q: Why was exp-014's velocity group suspected of leaking the target?
a: A 0.10 AUC jump from a single feature group looked too good, and the velocity window 'around' the observation date could include days after it, inside the 90-day label window.

q: Why should v2 numbers computed before 27 October 2026 be treated with caution?
a: Because the txn table feeds the velocity features and the September 2025 partitions were about 6% short until the backfill finished on 2026-10-27, so those v2 numbers used about 6% fewer September transactions.

q: Why do new accounts need separate treatment rather than the same model?
a: They have too little history for velocity or utilization features to mean much, and the model barely ranks them, yet they are 14% of the book and 21% of churners.

q: Why would the call tier shrink under churn-xgb-v3 at the current cuts?
a: Because churn-xgb-v3's scores are less extreme, with fewer accounts above 0.50, so the call tier would fall from 3.8% to about 2.9% of the book.
